newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WESTERN AUSTRALIA CLOSE IN AGAINST NSW.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WESTERN AUSTRALIA CLOSE IN AGAINST NSW.

text.p: Western Australia were poised to record a crushing victory against New South Wales after dominating the third day at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Saturday.
Chasing a target of 220 to win, the visitors cruised to 166 for one at close of play with one day left to play.
Opener Michael Hussey ended the day unbeaten on 58 alongside Australia test batsman Justin Langer on 42 not out.
Western Australia scored 244 after dismissing New South Wales for 126 in their first innings. The home side fought back with a score of 337 to set their opponents a victory target.
In Melbourne, Tasmania took control of their match against Victoria by racing to 182 for three at close of play on the third day after hitting 359 for seven declared in their first innings.
Victoria scored 284 for nine in their first innings at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
South Australia batsman Darren Lehmann hit 255, his highest first class score, to steer the home side to an imposing 527 for six declared at Adelaide Oval.
Queensland were struggling on 143 for six in reply at close of play on the second day.
